subject: History
description: Covers Iltutmish, Alauddin Khilji market reforms, and Tughlaq capital shift.

questions.stem: Who is generally considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate, having shifted the capital from Lahore to Delhi and saving it from Mongol invasions?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: While Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, he ruled from Lahore and his reign was very short (4 years). It was his son-in-law, Shams-ud-din Iltutmish, who shifted the capital to Delhi, organized the administration, introduced the standard silver coin (Tanka) and copper coin (Jital), and diplomatically saved India from the wrath of Genghis Khan by refusing asylum to a fleeing Central Asian prince. Therefore, historians call him the real founder.
DECOY BUSTING: Aibak was the first ruler but not the consolidator. Razia was Iltutmish's daughter (the only female ruler). Balban was a later Mamluk ruler known for his iron-fisted "blood and iron" policy.
EXAM INSIGHT: Iltutmish also created the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (The Group of Forty), an elite corps of Turkish nobles who held immense power, which Balban later brutally destroyed to centralize his own authority.

questions.stem: Which Sultan of Delhi implemented strict market control and price regulation policies to maintain a massive standing army without bankrupting the state treasury?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Alauddin Khilji maintained the largest standing army of the Delhi Sultanate to defend against Mongol invasions and to fund his rapid conquests of South India. To pay this massive army without draining the treasury, he fixed the prices of all essential commodities (grains, cloth, horses, slaves) at artificially low rates in Delhi. He appointed strict market controllers (Shahna-i-Mandi) and spies (Munhiyans) to ensure merchants didn't hoard or overcharge.
DECOY BUSTING: Muhammad bin Tughlaq is famous for his disastrous experiments (shifting capital to Daulatabad, token currency). Firoz Shah Tughlaq built many canals and cities. Sikandar Lodi founded the city of Agra.
EXAM INSIGHT: Alauddin was also the first Sultan to pay his soldiers entirely in cash (rather than land grants/iqtas) and introduced the branding of horses (Dagh) and maintaining a descriptive roll of soldiers (Huliya) to prevent corruption in the army.

questions.stem: The ambitious but disastrous decision to shift the capital of the Sultanate from Delhi to Devagiri (renamed Daulatabad) in the Deccan was taken by:
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (often called the 'Mad Sultan' or a visionary ahead of his time) shifted his capital to Daulatabad (in modern Maharashtra) in 1327. He reasoned that Daulatabad was centrally located and would allow him to control the newly conquered South Indian territories while being safe from Mongol invasions in the North. However, he ordered the entire population of Delhi to march 1,500 km south, leading to immense suffering and death.
DECOY BUSTING: Alauddin Khilji conquered the Deccan but ruled from Delhi. Balban never crossed the Vindhyas. Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan, defeated by Babur.
EXAM INSIGHT: Realizing his mistake when he couldn't control rebellions in the North from the South, Tughlaq ordered everyone back to Delhi a few years later. His other famous failed experiment was introducing 'Token Currency' (copper/brass coins meant to have the value of silver), which led to massive counterfeiting in every household.
